chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Hudhayl ibn Ḥanān, the brother of Jaʿfar ibn Ḥanān al-Ṣayrafī, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: I gave some money to my brother Jaʿfar, and he gives me from it what I spend, what I perform hajj with, and what I give in charity. I asked those around us, and they mentioned that this is invalid and not halal, and I would love to conclude in this matter with your statement.
So he said: Did he use to give to you before you handed your money over to him? I said: Yes. He said: Take from him what he gives you, and eat, and drink, and perform hajj, and give in charity.
Then when you arrive in Iraq, say: Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad has given me this ruling.

key_terms.أَتَصَدَّقُ: I give in charity, meaning voluntary charitable spending
key_terms.أَحُجُّ: I perform hajj, indicating use of the funds for pilgrimage
key_terms.أَفْتَانِي: he gave me a legal ruling or fatwa
key_terms.دَفَعْتُ: I handed over or entrusted, referring here to transferring money to another person
key_terms.فَاسِدٌ: invalid or unsound, describing the alleged legal problem in the transaction
key_terms.لَا يَحِلُّ: not halal or not permissible under the law
key_terms.مَالًا: wealth or money, the property placed with the brother

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to benefit from money or gifts given by someone after entrusting them with your wealth?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal question about money entrusted to a relative and the permissibility of benefiting from what that relative gives in return. Imam Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام permits taking such benefits when the giving was already an established practice before the transfer of wealth, indicating a distinction relevant to financial law and lawful use of property.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3704 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Hudhayl ibn Hanan, the brother of Ja'far ibn Hanan, the money changer, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (as), "I gave my brother Ja'far some money, and he gives me from it what I spend, perform Hajj with, and give in charity. I asked the people around us, and they said that this is invalid and not permissible. I wish to follow your guidance in this matter."

Imam (as) said: "Did he use to give to you before you entrusted him with your money?"
I said: "Yes."
Imam (as) said: "Then take what he gives you, eat, drink, perform Hajj, and give in charity.
And when you return to Iraq, say, 'Ja'far ibn Muhammad (as) has given me this ruling.'"
